english.note: Use 好 as the all-purpose colloquial intensifier before adjectives and other descriptive expressions.
Use this before an adjective when English means very, as in being very angry or very tired.
This is the all-purpose spoken choice before an adjective or stative verb.
Use this as the everyday degree adverb for wanting or needing something very much.
This is the all-purpose choice for expressing a very great degree, as in being deeply concerned.
Use this as the everyday intensifier for feeling or doing something very much, rather than for physical force.
Use this as the all-purpose spoken intensifier for “very,” “extremely,” or “to a great extent.”
This is the all-purpose spoken choice for meaning “very” or “extremely,” as in “highly visible.”
This is the all-purpose spoken degree adverb for saying someone or something is extremely so.
For “very,” 好 is the all-purpose spoken choice before an adjective.
This is the all-purpose everyday intensifier for saying that something is very or extremely so.
This is the all-purpose spoken choice for saying that something is extremely so.
This is the all-purpose spoken intensifier before adjectives and many verb phrases when “hugely” means to a very great extent.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that you enjoy, like, or feel something to a very great degree.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for expressing a very high degree, as in being acutely aware.
This is the everyday all-purpose intensifier before an adjective or stative predicate, as in 好開心.
This is the all-purpose everyday choice for saying that someone did or felt something immensely.
This is the all-purpose casual intensifier for strong effects such as being profoundly troubled.
This is the all-purpose choice for expressing a great degree, including positive statements and many negative ones such as 唔係好鍾意.
Use this for the degree sense before an adjective or verb, especially in combinations such as 好開心 or 好想去.
Use this before an adjective when “absolutely” means simply “very,” as in 好叻 or 好靚.
Use this before an adjective when “seriously” means “very” or “to a great degree.”
Use 好 as the everyday spoken choice for ‘very’ before an adjective.
Use 好 before an adjective or adverb when “well” means to a significant degree, as in 好出名 for “well known.”
Use this before an adjective or verb for plain “very” or “so much,” especially in a positive or negative statement.
Use this before an adjective when truly means very or extremely.
